messages:
incident-bot: P1 page triggered for AZ-east-4 — elevated client errors and timeouts across dual-stack frontends. Auto-detect suggests packet loss on IPv6 path, possible PMTUD/fragmentation. Paging on-call: @sarah-net and @jordan-sre.

incident-bot: Alert details: 13:02 UTC spike in 5xx for customers using eu-west and us-east via AZ-east-4. Affected routes: v6-prefixed frontends and some DNS responses failing to reach recursive resolvers.

sarah-net: On it. Seeing a surge of ICMP unreachable fragments on our v4->v6 transit. Could be MTU-related. Anyone changed MTU or introduced jumbo frame policy in az-east-4?

jordan-sre: Not from infra side. No config pushes last 24h. We saw increased 499/504s from downstream LB health checks.

sarah-net: Captured tcpdump from a border node (snippet):
```
20:02:11.123456 IP6 host1 > host2: Flags [P.], seq 1:1451, ack 1, win 65535, length 1450
20:02:11.123789 ICMP6, parameter problem, next-hop MTU 1280 from gateway
20:02:11.124000 IP host1 > host2: frag 0: DF??? (mtu clash)
```
This looks like PMTUD blackhole behavior — Path MTU reduced to 1280 but endpoints still sending larger segments.

lee-eng: Quick question: are we seeing application-layer retries or immediate client failures? Prod logs show long tail latencies then 502.

jordan-sre: From ingress LB logs: majority of failures on connections using IPv6. IPv4 steady. 90% of affected requests used v6.

taylor-prod: Customer impact: two large customers in EU reported intermittent failed uploads and stalled websockets. Support tickets increasing. Noting chest pain.

morgan-support: Tickets: #8451, #8457 — both show errors like `upstream closed connection without response` and `client timed out while waiting for response`. They include client IPs that are v6.

sarah-net: Hypothesis: an underlying router applied an MSS/MTU clamp change or is dropping ICMPv6 Packet Too Big messages. Immediate mitigation options: 1) apply an ingress MSS clamp at our edge (prevent large segments over v6), 2) adjust BGP path to steer traffic away from problematic transit for v6, 3) DNS steer to prefer IPv4 for affected frontends while we investigate.

jordan-sre: Priorities: reduce customer impact fast. I can push MSS clamp on the edge and change LB health to prefer IPv4 if we can do a DNS fallback quickly. Which is quickest?

sarah-net: MSS clamp should be quick — doing it now as emergency change on edge instances. Command (applied via runbook):
```
# on edge node
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
Applying to the egress chain across the AZ-east-4 fleet. Will flush in 30m unless rollback needed.

jordan-sre: Rolling that to canary pool (20% of edge instances) now. Monitoring logs.

incident-bot: Change recorded: iptables MSS clamp applied to edge-canary-1..4 by sarah-net at 13:12 UTC.

lee-eng: Canary metrics: IPv6 error rate dropped ~55% in canary pool within 2m. Latency for affected customers improved.

sarah-net: Good sign. Starting a gradual rollout across AZ-east-4.

taylor-prod: Initiating DNS steering to reduce new connections using AAAA where possible for impacted frontends. We can lower AAAA priority for zone-front-* for 10m to allow clients to pick A records. Ops, please coordinate TTLs.

jordan-sre: Lowered AAAA weight in our Traffic Steering config for zone-front-eu and zone-front-us for AZ-east-4 to 0.5 at 13:18 UTC; TTL set to 30s.

incident-bot: DNS change propagated via control plane; external resolvers ~30-90s to honor TTL. Recorded by pagerduty.

morgan-support: Customer-impact update: ticket #8451 reports uploads resumed after 13:20 UTC. #8457 still reporting occasional stalls but much improved.

sarah-net: Networking team will trace to upstream transit provider to confirm whether they suppressed ICMPv6 PTB or implemented an MTU clamp causing PMTUD to fail. Opening a support case with Provider-X now (case 992311).

lee-eng: Also let's capture pcap for a problematic flow and share with Provider-X. Make sure to scrub customer IPs before uploading.

jordan-sre: On-call handoff coming up in 25m. @taylor-prod, @morgan-support — I'll be passing to night shift. Current mitigation: MSS clamp rolled to 100% in AZ-east-4 edges, DNS AAAA weight reduced, monitoring shows errors down ~70% cluster-wide.

taylor-prod: Acknowledged. Logging actions in incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-3342 (link). Putting notice in status page: "Partial IPv6 routing disruption in AZ-east-4, mitigation in progress".

incident-bot: PagerDuty: On-call handoff scheduled to jordan-sre -> night-sre at 13:45 UTC.

morgan-support: Noting customers with strict IPv6-only environments might still see issues; added workaround steps for customers: use IPv4 endpoint or retry with smaller chunk sizes.

sarah-net: Provider-X responded: they observe a hardware bug on a subset of their routers causing suppression of ICMPv6 PTB for certain path combinations when jumbo frames enabled on customer side. Proposed immediate action from provider: disable jumbo-negotiate on their peer fabric (ETA 40m) or we continue with MSS clamp + DNS steering.

jordan-sre: Given customer impact and short-term mitigation working, let's keep MSS clamp and DNS steering until provider confirms fix. After provider patch, we'll run controlled rollback: first remove DNS steering, then gradually disable MSS clamp in canary.

lee-eng: Add a regression test to ensure that when PMTUD fails we fallback to MSS clamp automatically for future deployments. Filing a follow-up with eng-runtime.

taylor-prod: Status update to customers posted at 13:36 UTC. No data loss, degraded connectivity for IPv6 flows only. Expecting provider fix in ~40m.

incident-bot: Incident severity remains P1. Next update scheduled in 20m or on major state change.

jordan-sre: Handoff: night-sre please watch for any rise in 5xx on IPv6, and keep provider case open. If error rate rises >20% of baseline, escalate to oncall-net and paging.

night-sre: Acknowledged. Taking channel. Good job team, leave notes for postmortem — include timestamps of MSS clamp and DNS change.

morgan-support: Closing notes: tracked impacted customers, provided manual IPv4 endpoints. Will follow up once provider confirms fix.

incident-bot: Provider-X updated case 992311: firmware patch scheduled for 14:08 UTC; they will apply to affected routers in AZ-east-4. Will post after completion.

sarah-net: After provider patch, we'll run pcap & health checks and then lift MSS clamp if no regressions for 30m.

(13:52 UTC) incident-bot: Provider-X reports patch applied to targeted routers. Monitoring for 30m.

(14:25 UTC) jordan-sre: 30m monitoring complete. No spike in IPv6 errors. Rolling back MSS clamp in canary now, then full rollback in 10m if stable.

(14:40 UTC) incident-bot: MSS clamp removed across AZ-east-4 by sarah-net at 14:37 UTC. DNS steering reverted at 14:38 UTC.

(14:45 UTC) taylor-prod: Status page updated: "Service restored to normal in AZ-east-4; root cause: ISP router firmware bug affecting ICMPv6 PTB handling.", customers notified.

(14:50 UTC) jordan-sre: Postmortem checklist created and assigned to sarah-net, lee-eng, and taylor-prod. Will include timeline, actions, provider RCA, and follow-ups: automated MSS fallback, more robust IPv6 healthchecks, and improved on-call playbook.

(15:00 UTC) incident-bot: Incident transitioned to post-incident review. Thread closed for live mitigation.
